hook_text: Cell, switch, bulb, two wires. Light. Pull one clip off and watch the whole thing die.
clip_script: Clip a cell to a switch, the switch to a bulb, the bulb back to the cell. Press. Light. Now pull one clip off anywhere. Dark. Electricity only moves round a complete loop; one gap and it all stops. A switch is just a gap you control. Swap the bulb for a buzzer and connect it backwards: silence. Buzzers are one-way; bulbs do not care. Open the switch and bridge it with a nail: light. Foil: light. Plastic ruler: nothing. Metals conduct, plastic insulates, which is why wire is copper in a plastic jacket. Now draw it, not as a picture but as symbols: long and short line for the cell, a hinged gap for the switch, a circle with a cross for the bulb, straight ruled lines for wires. That drawing can be built by anyone on Earth.
visual_style: Whiteboard loop lighting and dying as a clip comes off; a row of materials across a gap; the circuit redrawn in clean symbols.
mood: Hands-on and snappy, every test with a visible result.
pacing: Build, break, fix; quick material run; slow on the final diagram.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the circuit with your group, then draw it.
